title: Beni Mellal city and foothills, 8 Oct to 20 Oct 2026
summary: Between 8 Oct and 20 Oct 2026 the radar shows almost no change around Beni Mellal: 0.36 km2 turned brighter and 0.55 km2 darker in HV. Both dates carry the same flag, so they share the October offset and every number here should be read with low confidence.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 12 days mean HV moved by -0.07 dB and mean HH by -0.14 dB. In HV, 0.36 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.55 km2 darker; in HH, 0.4 km2 turned brighter and 0.47 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The changing fields fell 0.39 dB in HV, with 0.2 km2 darker. Rough dry ground and fields had 0.11 km2 brighter and 0.17 km2 darker in HV, and trees, shrub and rugged slopes 0.11 km2 brighter and 0.11 km2 darker. Built-up land fell 0.16 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the steady scene: both dates carry the same October offset, so it cancels out between them; reprocessed files would show it. Possible cause for the darker fields: a few plots harvested or ploughed; a field visit would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Both dates carry a flag: backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median, a possible processing offset or widespread wet conditions. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Do not use this pair on its own. Compare each October date with an unflagged summer date, and ask NASA whether the October products will be reprocessed.
